questionText: The man ___ lives here is nice.

frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'qui' for both people and things (as subject). English distinguishes.

questionText: The book ___ is on the table is mine.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Le livre qui est sur la table
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The book which is on the table

questionText: This is the house ___ I was born.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: La maison où je suis né
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The house where I was born

questionText: The girl ___ you met is my sister.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: La fille que tu as rencontrée

questionText: The car ___ I bought is red.
I know a man ___ can speak 5 languages.
The pen ___ you gave me is blue.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Le stylo que tu m'as donné
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The pen that you gave me

questionText: This is the school ___ I study.
The woman ___ called you is waiting.
The dog ___ barked is loud.
I have a friend ___ lives in London.
The movie ___ we watched was good.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Le film que nous avons regardé

questionText: This is the city ___ I work.
The boy ___ is playing is my brother.
The phone ___ I lost was new.
People ___ live in glass houses shouldn't throw stones.
The cake ___ she made was delicious.
That is the shop ___ I bought my shoes.
The teacher ___ teaches English is nice.
The letter ___ arrived today is for you.
The man ___ car was stolen is angry.
The reason ___ I am late is traffic.
The day ___ we met was sunny.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Le jour où nous nous sommes rencontrés
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: French uses 'où' (where) for time too. English uses 'when'.

questionText: The person to ___ I spoke was helpful.
feedback: Correct! After a preposition, use 'whom' for people (formal).

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: La personne à qui j'ai parlé
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The person to whom I spoke

questionText: Everything ___ he said is true.
I don't know ___ to do.
feedback: Correct! Indirect question / Nominal relative clause.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Je ne sais pas quoi faire
frenchComparison.englishStructure: I don't know what to do

questionText: The hotel, ___ was expensive, was nice.
feedback: Correct! Non-defining clause (with commas) must use 'which', not 'that'.

questionText: My brother, ___ lives in Paris, is a doctor.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Mon frère, qui vit à Paris...
frenchComparison.englishStructure: My brother, who lives in Paris...

questionText: The book ___ cover is torn.
This is ___ I want.
The woman ___ bag was stolen.
That is the reason ___ he left.
I remember the time ___ we went there.
The man with ___ I work.

frenchComparison.englishStructure: The man with whom I work

questionText: All ___ glitters is not gold.
Tell me ___ you want.
feedback: Correct! Tell me the thing that...

questionText: My car, ___ is old, runs well.
Mr. Smith, ___ is a teacher, lives here.

frenchComparison.englishStructure: Mr. Smith, who is a teacher...

questionText: A house ___ roof is red.
___ he says is important.
The man ___ I spoke to.
feedback: Correct! In informal English, 'who' is used and the preposition goes at the end.

frenchComparison.englishStructure: The man who I spoke to

visualHighlighting.incorrect: The man to who I spoke
visualHighlighting.correct: The man who I spoke to

questionText: The bed ___ I slept in.
feedback: Correct! 'Which' (or 'that') + preposition at end. 'Where' cannot be followed by a preposition.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Le lit dans lequel j'ai dormi
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The bed which I slept in

visualHighlighting.incorrect: The bed where I slept in
visualHighlighting.correct: The bed which I slept in

questionText: He said he was ill, ___ was a lie.
feedback: Correct! 'Which' refers to the whole previous clause.

questionText: The man ___ car I bought.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: L'homme dont j'ai acheté la voiture
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The man whose car I bought

questionText: The people, ___ were tired, went home.
He has two cars, ___ are red.
The reason ___ I did it is secret.
The way ___ he talks is funny.
feedback: Correct! 'The way that' or 'The way' (zero relative). 'The way how' is incorrect.

questionText: ___ needs help should ask.
You can eat ___ you like.
The girl ___ I was sitting next to.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: La fille à côté de qui...
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The girl who I was sitting next to

visualHighlighting.incorrect: next to who I was sitting
visualHighlighting.correct: who I was sitting next to

questionText: The house ___ I live in.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: La maison dans laquelle je vis
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The house which I live in

visualHighlighting.incorrect: The house where I live in
visualHighlighting.correct: The house which I live in
